about.title: Rancho Cordova Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Nine people died on Rancho Cordova streets in 2025, according to public collision records. Behind each of those numbers is a household in Sacramento County that suddenly has to plan a funeral, cover bills, and figure out what comes next without the person who used to help carry the load. If that is where you find yourself, a wrongful death claim is one way California law allows surviving family to seek accountability. It is a civil case, entirely separate from anything the police or district attorney may pursue, and it can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed. The Rancho Cordova corridors with the highest collision counts in the data include Sunrise Boulevard, Folsom Boulevard, Coloma Road and Zinfandel Drive, with reported crashes clustering on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that introduces you to an independent attorney who handles wrongful death matters and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless something is recovered.

whyChoose.title: What Rancho Cordova Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Only certain family members can file
items.desc: California gives a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in some circumstances. An attorney can sort out who in your family has standing before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock is two years, sometimes less
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death. If a government entity such as the city, county or state may be responsible, the window to give notice is considerably shorter, so waiting is risky.

items.title: Losses go beyond the funeral bill
items.desc: Recoverable damages can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. A civil claim is separate from any criminal case and does not depend on one being filed.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash near Zinfandel Drive. Who is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California law puts the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children first in line. If none exist, the right can pass to others who would inherit, and certain financially dependent relatives may qualify as well. Because families are rarely simple, an attorney will usually confirm standing early so the right people are named from the start.

items.question: How long do we have to act in Sacramento County?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death, not the date of the crash. If a public agency might share fault, for example through a city-owned vehicle or a road maintenance issue, a formal claim typically has to be presented within a much shorter period. Missing either deadline can end the case before it begins.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from anything the district attorney does. Your family can pursue it even if charges are reduced, dropped or never filed, and the outcome of one case does not automatically decide the other.
